picks.title: Seeing the unseen: A new tool visualizes hidden structures in complex biological data
picks.excerpt: University of Basel researchers released Bonsai, which renders high-dimensional single-cell data as branching trees instead of flat 2D maps, preserving true distances between cells. The tool surfaced a previously unknown natural killer cell subtype in human blood.
picks.rationale: A released visualization tool that proves a representation choice — trees over flattened 2D maps — can reveal a cell type nobody had seen; the rare science story that is really about design of the view.

picks.title: We still don't know how people are really using AI
picks.excerpt: A new independent research project, the AI Observatory, aggregates consented real conversations with Claude and Gemini to build a public picture of AI use. It found nearly half of conversations are non-work — health, relationships, sensitive topics — categories that vendor usage reports largely omit.
picks.rationale: First vendor-independent usage dataset: if half of real AI use is personal rather than work, every product assumption built on vendor usage reports is mis-aimed.

picks.title: AI has created a shadow medical system
picks.excerpt: More than 40 million Americans ask ChatGPT a health question every day, almost entirely outside clinical settings. Paired with direct-to-consumer labs and AI-generated prescriptions, that has quietly assembled a parallel care system with no physician oversight or accountability.
picks.rationale: Documents an entire care system that assembled itself out of consumer AI products — the clearest case study yet of interface decisions becoming public-health infrastructure.

picks.title: AI-designed "intrabodies" could unlock new treatments for Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and MND
picks.excerpt: University of Essex researchers used AI to redesign ordinary antibodies into tiny fragments that stay stable and functional inside living human cells, targeting disease proteins that conventional antibodies can't reach. Published in Nature Communications, the redesigned molecules will be released freely to other labs.
picks.rationale: AI protein design crossing into the cell interior — a peer-reviewed result with the designed molecules released free to other labs, so it compounds immediately.

picks.title: Quantum X Labs Tests AI Quantum Error Decoder on Google Hardware Dataset
picks.excerpt: Quantum X Labs reported that its AI-driven surface-code decoder improved accuracy on Google's public real-hardware dataset while having been trained purely on synthetic data. Transferring from simulation to physical qubits without hardware-specific retraining is the hard part of the problem.
picks.rationale: Synthetic-only training that survives contact with real qubits is the sim-to-real result quantum error correction has been waiting for, and it is freshest item in the pool.
